item.title: Induction head
item.description:
An induction head is a two-layer attention sub-circuit that completes recurring sequences via pattern matching: given context ... [A] [B] ... [A], it predicts that [B] follows the current [A].

Induction heads are considered the primary mechanistic engine driving in-context learning in Transformers. To implement this algorithm across layers, heads must compose by reading each other’s outputs from the residual stream.

The Algorithmic Goal of an Induction Head

Suppose the input sequence contains:

…[A]⏟i−1 [B]⏟i … [A]⏟j \dots \underbrace{\text{[A]}}_{i-1} \ \underbrace{\text{[B]}}_{i} \ \dots \ \underbrace{\text{[A]}}_{j} …i−1[A]​​ i[B]​​ … j[A]​​

The current token is at position jjj (which is [A]). To predict that [B] comes next, the network must:

  1. Search backward in the context for an earlier occurrence of token [A].
  2. Find the token that immediately followed that earlier [A] (which is [B] at position iii).
  3. Copy [B] to the current prediction at position jjj.

A single attention layer cannot do this on its own:

  • At position iii (where [B] is located), the token [B] has no native awareness that token [A] occurred immediately before it, unless another head or embedding shifted that information into position iii.
  • A 1-layer model can implement a “previous-token head” or a “copy-current-token head”, but it cannot perform “look for previous token matching current token, and extract the next token.”

This requires a circuit consisting of at least two heads across two distinct layers:

  • Head 1 (Layer 0 or early layer): A Previous-Token Head (H1H_1H1​).
  • Head 2 (Layer 1 or downstream layer): An Induction Head (H2H_2H2​).

The Attention Composition Framework

In a multi-layer Transformer, Layer 1 receives the residual stream modified by Layer 0:

x(1)=x(0)+∑h∈L0headh(x(0)) x^{(1)} = x^{(0)} + \sum_{h \in L_0} \text{head}_h(x^{(0)}) x(1)=x(0)+h∈L0​∑​headh​(x(0))

When head H2H_2H2​ in Layer 1 runs, its input vector xxx contains terms from H1H_1H1​’s OV output: WOV(1)xW_{OV}^{(1)} xWOV(1)​x. Expanding the inputs to H2H_2H2​ reveals three distinct ways an upstream head can feed into a downstream head:

Upstream Head H1 (Layer 0)
|
[W_OV]
| (Residual Stream)
+-----------------------+-----------------------+
| | |
v v v
[W_Q] [W_K] [W_V]
| | |
Downstream Head H2 Q-Input Downstream Head H2 K-Input Downstream Head H2 V-Input
(Q-Composition) (K-Composition) (V-Composition)
  1. Q-Composition: H1H_1H1​’s output feeds into H2H_2H2​’s Query projection: WQ(2)(WOV(1)x)=(WQ(2)WOV(1))x W_Q^{(2)} \left( W_{OV}^{(1)} x \right) = \left( W_Q^{(2)} W_{OV}^{(1)} \right) x WQ(2)​(WOV(1)​x)=(WQ(2)​WOV(1)​)x
  2. K-Composition: H1H_1H1​’s output feeds into H2H_2H2​’s Key projection: WK(2)(WOV(1)x)=(WK(2)WOV(1))x W_K^{(2)} \left( W_{OV}^{(1)} x \right) = \left( W_K^{(2)} W_{OV}^{(1)} \right) x WK(2)​(WOV(1)​x)=(WK(2)​WOV(1)​)x
  3. V-Composition: H1H_1H1​’s output feeds into H2H_2H2​’s Value projection: WV(2)(WOV(1)x)=(WV(2)WOV(1))x W_V^{(2)} \left( W_{OV}^{(1)} x \right) = \left( W_V^{(2)} W_{OV}^{(1)} \right) x WV(2)​(WOV(1)​x)=(WV(2)​WOV(1)​)x

Step-by-Step: How Induction Heads Work

The standard induction circuit uses K-Composition (or Q-Composition) to set up the attention pattern, followed by the OV circuit to copy the token.

Step 1: Head H1H_1H1​ acts as a Previous-Token Head (Layer 0)

Head H1H_1H1​ attends from position iii to position i−1i-1i−1 (often relying on positional embeddings/RoPE in its QK circuit):

  • At position iii (which holds [B]), H1H_1H1​ reads the representation of [A] from position i−1i-1i−1.
  • H1H_1H1​’s OV circuit writes a vector containing the identity of [A] directly into the residual stream at position iii: xi(1)≈xi(0)+WOV(1)xi−1(0) x_i^{(1)} \approx x_i^{(0)} + W_{OV}^{(1)} x_{i-1}^{(0)} xi(1)​≈xi(0)​+WOV(1)​xi−1(0)​
  • Result: Position iii (token [B]) now carries a tag in the residual stream saying “I was preceded by token [A]”.

Step 2: Head H2H_2H2​ uses K-Composition to Match Queries and Keys (Layer 1)

At the current position jjj, the token is [A]. Head H2H_2H2​’s Query vector at position jjj is computed directly from [A]:

qj=WQ(2)xj≈WQ(2)x[A] q_j = W_Q^{(2)} x_j \approx W_Q^{(2)} x_{\text{[A]}} qj​=WQ(2)​xj​≈WQ(2)​x[A]​

Meanwhile, for all earlier positions iii, Head H2H_2H2​’s Key vector receives the residual stream containing H1H_1H1​’s output via K-composition:

ki=WK(2)xi(1)=WK(2)(xi(0)+WOV(1)xi−1(0))=WK(2)xi(0)+WK(2)WOV(1)xi−1(0)⏟K-Composition Term k_i = W_K^{(2)} x_i^{(1)} = W_K^{(2)} \left( x_i^{(0)} + W_{OV}^{(1)} x_{i-1}^{(0)} \right) = W_K^{(2)} x_i^{(0)} + \underbrace{W_K^{(2)} W_{OV}^{(1)} x_{i-1}^{(0)}}_{\text{K-Composition Term}} ki​=WK(2)​xi(1)​=WK(2)​(xi(0)​+WOV(1)​xi−1(0)​)=WK(2)​xi(0)​+K-Composition TermWK(2)​WOV(1)​xi−1(0)​​​

The QK score between current position jjj and prior position iii contains the bilinear term:

scorej,i∝qj⊤ki⊃(WQ(2)x[A])⊤(WK(2)WOV(1)xi−1(0))=x[A]⊤((WQ(2))⊤WK(2)WOV(1))xi−1(0) \text{score}_{j,i} \propto q_j^\top k_i \supset \left( W_Q^{(2)} x_{\text{[A]}} \right)^\top \left( W_K^{(2)} W_{OV}^{(1)} x_{i-1}^{(0)} \right) = x_{\text{[A]}}^\top \left( (W_Q^{(2)})^\top W_K^{(2)} W_{OV}^{(1)} \right) x_{i-1}^{(0)} scorej,i​∝qj⊤​ki​⊃(WQ(2)​x[A]​)⊤(WK(2)​WOV(1)​xi−1(0)​)=x[A]⊤​((WQ(2)​)⊤WK(2)​WOV(1)​)xi−1(0)​

Because xi−1(0)x_{i-1}^{(0)}xi−1(0)​ is also token [A], the combined composition matrix:

CK=(WQ(2))⊤WK(2)WOV(1) C_K = (W_Q^{(2)})^\top W_K^{(2)} W_{OV}^{(1)} CK​=(WQ(2)​)⊤WK(2)​WOV(1)​

acts as an identity/match detector between token jjj and token i−1i-1i−1.

When token jjj matches token i−1i-1i−1 (both are [A]), the score spikes positively, causing Head H2H_2H2​ at position jjj to place nearly all its attention weight on position iii (the token [B]).

Step 3: Copying via H2H_2H2​’s OV Circuit

Once H2H_2H2​ attends to position iii, its own Value and Output matrices execute a copying operation:

outputj=WO(2)WV(2)xi \text{output}_j = W_O^{(2)} W_V^{(2)} x_i outputj​=WO(2)​WV(2)​xi​

Since xix_ixi​ holds [B], WOV(2)=WO(2)WV(2)W_{OV}^{(2)} = W_O^{(2)} W_V^{(2)}WOV(2)​=WO(2)​WV(2)​ projects the token embedding of [B] into the direction of the residual stream that the final unembedding matrix (WUW_UWU​) decodes as [B].

Q-Composition vs. K-Composition

Induction heads can be implemented using either mechanism depending on how the model factors the problem:

Property K-Composition Induction Q-Composition Induction
Upstream Head (H1H_1H1​) Writes “previous token is [A]” into position iii ([B]). Writes “subsequent token should match [A]” into position jjj.
Composed Matrix WK(2)WOV(1)W_K^{(2)}W_{OV}^{(1)}WK(2)​WOV(1)​ WQ(2)WOV(1)W_Q^{(2)}W_{OV}^{(1)}WQ(2)​WOV(1)​
Mechanistic Role Changes what key is presented at candidate positions iii. Changes what query is searched for by current position jjj.
Intuition Query searches for “who had token [A] before them?” Key responds “I did!” Query says “I am looking for the token following [A]”. Key says “I am token [B]”.

In empirical circuits research (e.g., in toy models and open LLMs), K-composition is the dominant form observed for induction heads, though mixed variants (both Q- and K-composition active simultaneously) also occur.

Detecting Composition in the Wild

To confirm whether two heads H1H_1H1​ and H2H_2H2​ are actually composing rather than operating independently, interpretability researchers use two quantitative tests:

  1. Path Patching (Activation Patching): Run the model on a repeated sequence [A][B] ... [A]. Intercept the output of H1H_1H1​ entering H2H_2H2​’s KKK-input and replace it with corrupted/random activations. If the model’s ability to predict [B] vanishes, H2H_2H2​ causally depends on H1H_1H1​ via K-composition.
  2. Matrix Norm Metrics: Measure the Frobenius norm of the product matrix: ∥WK(2)WOV(1)∥F \Vert{} W_K^{(2)} W_{OV}^{(1)} \Vert{}_F ∥WK(2)​WOV(1)​∥F​ Compare this against a baseline where the weight matrices are randomly rotated. In true induction heads, the norm is significantly higher than chance, indicating that WK(2)W_K^{(2)}WK(2)​ specifically aligns with the subspace output by WOV(1)W_{OV}^{(1)}WOV(1)​.

item.title: QK OV circuit
item.description:
Mechanistic interpretability treats neural networks not as black boxes, but as computational graphs where weights and activations can be reverse-engineered into human-understandable algorithms.

In the mathematical framework popularized by Anthropic (Elhage et al., A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits), an attention layer is analyzed without the intermediate token dimensions by factoring it into two independent, end-to-end operations:

  1. The QK (Query-Key) circuit: Determines where information moves.
  2. The OV (Output-Value) circuit: Determines what information moves.

The Residual Stream as a Communication Bus

In a decoder-only autoregressive Transformer, token representations live in an nmodeln_{\text{model}}nmodel​-dimensional space called the residual stream (x∈Rdmodelx \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}x∈Rdmodel​).

Layers read from the residual stream via linear projections and write back into it by addition:

xl=xl−1+∑h=1Hheadl,h(xl−1) x_{l} = x_{l-1} + \sum_{h=1}^{H} \text{head}_{l,h}(x_{l-1}) xl​=xl−1​+h=1∑H​headl,h​(xl−1​)

A standard multi-head attention head hhh uses four weight matrices:

  • WQ,WK∈Rdk×dmodelW_Q, W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times d_{\text{model}}}WQ​,WK​∈Rdk​×dmodel​
  • WV∈Rdv×dmodelW_V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_v \times d_{\text{model}}}WV​∈Rdv​×dmodel​
  • WO∈Rdmodel×dvW_O \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}WO​∈Rdmodel​×dv​

Usually, we think of attention sequentially:

  1. qi=WQxiq_i = W_Q x_iqi​=WQ​xi​, kj=WKxjk_j = W_K x_jkj​=WK​xj​
  2. Ai,j=softmaxj(qi⊤kjdk)A_{i,j} = \text{softmax}_j\left(\frac{q_i^\top k_j}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)Ai,j​=softmaxj​(dk​​qi⊤​kj​​)
  3. vj=WVxjv_j = W_V x_jvj​=WV​xj​
  4. head(x)i=WO∑jAi,jvj\text{head}(x)_i = W_O \sum_j A_{i,j} v_jhead(x)i​=WO​∑j​Ai,j​vj​

Mechanistic interpretability collapses the internal dimension (dkd_kdk​ or dvd_vdv​) into direct end-to-end bilinear maps on the residual stream.

1. The QK Circuit: Directing Attention

The attention score between query token at position iii and key token at position jjj (ignoring positional embeddings for a moment) is:

scorei,j=qi⊤kjdk=(WQxi)⊤(WKxj)dk=xi⊤WQ⊤WKxjdk \text{score}_{i,j} = \frac{q_i^\top k_j}{\sqrt{d_k}} = \frac{(W_Q x_i)^\top (W_K x_j)}{\sqrt{d_k}} = \frac{x_i^\top W_Q^\top W_K x_j}{\sqrt{d_k}} scorei,j​=dk​​qi⊤​kj​​=dk​​(WQ​xi​)⊤(WK​xj​)​=dk​​xi⊤​WQ⊤​WK​xj​​

We define the QK matrix as:

WQK=WQ⊤WK∈Rdmodel×dmodel W_{QK} = W_Q^\top W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_{\text{model}}} WQK​=WQ⊤​WK​∈Rdmodel​×dmodel​
  • Rank: WQKW_{QK}WQK​ has a maximum rank of dkd_kdk​ (typically 64 or 128), which is much smaller than dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​ (often 4096+). It acts as a low-rank bilinear form.
  • Interpretation: Given a feature subspace active in the query token (xix_ixi​) and a feature subspace active in the key token (xjx_jxj​), WQKW_{QK}WQK​ directly computes their compatibility score:
scorei,j∝xi⊤WQKxj \text{score}_{i,j} \propto x_i^\top W_{QK} x_j scorei,j​∝xi⊤​WQK​xj​
  • Function: It acts as an addressing system. The QK circuit reads queries and keys from the residual stream and outputs scalar logits over context positions, entirely agnostic to the semantic content being copied or transformed downstream.

2. The OV Circuit: Transforming Content

Once attention weights Ai,j∈[0,1]A_{i,j} \in [0, 1]Ai,j​∈[0,1] are computed, the head moves information from source position jjj to destination position iii. Looking at a single source position jjj:

contributionj=WO(WVxj)=(WOWV)xj \text{contribution}_j = W_O (W_V x_j) = (W_O W_V) x_j contributionj​=WO​(WV​xj​)=(WO​WV​)xj​

We define the OV matrix as:

WOV=WOWV∈Rdmodel×dmodel W_{OV} = W_O W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_{\text{model}}} WOV​=WO​WV​∈Rdmodel​×dmodel​
  • Rank: Like WQKW_{QK}WQK​, WOVW_{OV}WOV​ has a rank bounded by dv≪dmodeld_v \ll d_{\text{model}}dv​≪dmodel​.
  • Interpretation: WOVW_{OV}WOV​ is a linear map that reads a low-rank subspace from the residual stream at the source position and writes another low-rank subspace directly into the residual stream at the destination position.
  • Function: It dictates what features get extracted from the source and in what direction they are written into the target. Crucially, WOVW_{OV}WOV​ has zero influence on which positions are attended to—it simply specifies the payload.

Complete Head Formulation

Putting both circuits together, the action of an attention head at destination token iii can be written without ever explicitly referencing the intermediate dkd_kdk​ or dvd_vdv​ dimensions:

head(x)i=∑j≤isoftmaxj(xi⊤WQKxjdk)⏟QK Circuit: Where to route⋅(WOVxj)⏟OV Circuit: What to write \text{head}(x)_i = \sum_{j \le i} \underbrace{\text{softmax}_j \left( \frac{x_i^\top W_{QK} x_j}{\sqrt{d_k}} \right)}_{\text{QK Circuit: Where to route}} \cdot \underbrace{\left( W_{OV} x_j \right)}_{\text{OV Circuit: What to write}} head(x)i​=j≤i∑​QK Circuit: Where to routesoftmaxj​(dk​​xi⊤​WQK​xj​​)​​⋅OV Circuit: What to write(WOV​xj​)​​
Circuit Matrix Operation Role
QK WQK=WQ⊤WKW_{QK}=W_Q^\top W_KWQK​=WQ⊤​WK​ xi⊤WQKxj→Scalarx_i^\top W_{QK}x_j\to\text{Scalar}xi⊤​WQK​xj​→Scalar Computes attention pattern (source-destination affinity).
OV WOV=WOWVW_{OV}=W_OW_VWOV​=WO​WV​ WOVxj→RdmodelW_{OV}x_j\to\mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}WOV​xj​→Rdmodel​ Transports and rotates features from source to destination.

Why Factorize into QK and OV?

  1. Separation of Concerns: When analyzing trained models, an attention head can fail or succeed in two distinct ways:
    • Addressing failure: Looking at the wrong token (QK circuit issue).
      • Transmission failure: Looking at the right token but writing the wrong vector or projecting into an orthogonal subspace (OV circuit issue).
  2. Eigenvalue/SVD Analysis of WOVW_{OV}WOV​:
    • If WOVW_{OV}WOV​ has positive real eigenvalues, the head acts as an identity/copying head, reinforcing existing token features.
      • If it has negative real eigenvalues, it acts as an inhibition head, erasing or dampening certain directions in the residual stream.
  3. Composability Across Layers: In multi-layer models, the output of an early head’s OV circuit feeds into the input of a downstream head’s QK or OV circuit. This leads directly to induction heads and attention composition pathways (QQQ-composition, KKK-composition, and VVV-composition).

item.title: Superposition, privileged basis, double descent
item.description:
1. Basis & Basis-Free Operations

In mechanistic interpretability, operations within a Transformer are categorized by whether their behavior depends on the coordinate system chosen to represent the vector space:

  • Basis-Free (Rotational Invariance): An operation where rotating the vector space by an orthogonal matrix RRR (R⊤R=IR^\top R = IR⊤R=I) preserves the overall transformation, provided the weights are rotated accordingly.
  • Privileged Basis: An operation where individual coordinate axes (neurons) carry distinct mathematical and semantic meaning that cannot be rotated without breaking the computation.

The Residual Stream is Basis-Free

The residual stream vector x∈Rdmodelx \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}x∈Rdmodel​ does not have an intrinsic coordinate system. If you rotate the entire residual stream by an orthogonal transformation RRR:

x′=Rx x' = R x x′=Rx

The linear projections of an attention head (WQ,WK,WV,WOW_Q, W_K, W_V, W_OWQ​,WK​,WV​,WO​) adapt simply by multiplying by R⊤R^\topR⊤:

WQ′=WQR⊤,WK′=WKR⊤,WV′=WVR⊤,WO′=RWO W'_Q = W_Q R^\top, \quad W'_K = W_K R^\top, \quad W'_V = W_V R^\top, \quad W'_O = R W_O WQ′​=WQ​R⊤,WK′​=WK​R⊤,WV′​=WV​R⊤,WO′​=RWO​

The internal dot products are preserved:

(WQ′x′)⊤(WK′x′)=(WQR⊤Rx)⊤(WKR⊤Rx)=(WQx)⊤(WKx) (W'_Q x')^\top (W'_K x') = (W_Q R^\top R x)^\top (W_K R^\top R x) = (W_Q x)^\top (W_K x) (WQ′​x′)⊤(WK′​x′)=(WQ​R⊤Rx)⊤(WK​R⊤Rx)=(WQ​x)⊤(WK​x)

Similarly, layer normalization (up to minor coordinate scaling) and linear read/write operations treat all directions symmetrically. There is no special meaning to the kkk-th coordinate of the residual stream.

MLPs Introduce a Privileged Basis

The MLP blocks break rotational symmetry because activation functions (ReLU\text{ReLU}ReLU, GELU\text{GELU}GELU, SwiGLU\text{SwiGLU}SwiGLU) are applied element-wise:

MLP(x)=Wout σ(Winx+bin) \text{MLP}(x) = W_{\text{out}} \ \sigma(W_{\text{in}} x + b_{\text{in}}) MLP(x)=Wout​ σ(Win​x+bin​)

For an arbitrary orthogonal matrix RRR, non-linearities generally do not commute with rotation:

σ(Rz)≠R σ(z) \sigma(R z) \ne R \ \sigma(z) σ(Rz)=R σ(z)

Because σ\sigmaσ evaluates each scalar component along the standard coordinate axes independently:

  1. The hidden layer of an MLP has a privileged basis: the coordinate axes correspond directly to individual neurons.
  2. In contrast, the residual stream lacks a privileged basis, making it harder to assign individual dimensions to discrete features without techniques like Dictionary Learning / Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs).

2. Superposition

Superposition is the phenomenon where a neural network represents significantly more independent features than it has dimensions (M≫dM \gg dM≫d).

The Geometric Mechanism

If features were strictly orthogonal, a ddd-dimensional space could represent at most ddd features without mutual interference. However, in high dimensions, an exponentially large number of vectors can be almost orthogonal (a consequence of the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma and high-dimensional sphere packing):

⟨vi,vj⟩≈0for i≠j \langle v_i, v_j \rangle \approx 0 \quad \text{for } i \ne j ⟨vi​,vj​⟩≈0for i=j

When a model maps MMM features {fi}i=1M\{f_i\}_{i=1}^M{fi​}i=1M​ with activations ai≥0a_i \ge 0ai​≥0 into a ddd-dimensional space via unit feature directions vi∈Rdv_i \in \mathbb{R}^dvi​∈Rd:

x=∑i=1Maivi x = \sum_{i=1}^M a_i v_i x=i=1∑M​ai​vi​

To decode feature kkk, we project xxx onto vkv_kvk​:

a^k=⟨vk,x⟩=ak+∑i≠kai⟨vk,vi⟩ \hat{a}_k = \langle v_k, x \rangle = a_k + \sum_{i \ne k} a_i \langle v_k, v_i \rangle a^k​=⟨vk​,x⟩=ak​+i=k∑​ai​⟨vk​,vi​⟩

The second term ∑i≠kai⟨vk,vi⟩\sum_{i \ne k} a_i \langle v_k, v_i \rangle∑i=k​ai​⟨vk​,vi​⟩ acts as interference noise (crosstalk).

Why Superposition Works: Sparsity

Superposition is computationally viable when real-world features are sparse—meaning only a tiny fraction of features ai>0a_i > 0ai​>0 fire simultaneously for any single input:

  1. If most ai=0a_i = 0ai​=0, the sum of interference noise remains small.
  2. Non-linear thresholding (e.g., ReLU\text{ReLU}ReLU) can clear out small interference ripples: ReLU(a^k−τ)≈ak \text{ReLU}(\hat{a}_k - \tau) \approx a_k ReLU(a^k​−τ)≈ak​

Polysemanticity

Superposition directly causes polysemanticity: because feature directions are not aligned with standard basis vectors, individual neurons (the basis vectors) end up projecting onto multiple unrelated feature directions. Inspecting a single neuron activation reveals that it activates for multiple distinct, unrelated concepts.

3. Double Descent

Double descent is a generalization phenomenon that reconciles classical statistical learning theory with the empirical success of deep, overparameterized neural networks.

 ```

Risk / Test Error | | Underfitting Interpolation Peak | \ /
| \ /
| Classical \ Overfitting/ \ Modern Overparameterized | U-Curve \ Spike / \ Regime | \ / -—————– | _______/ +————————————————————> Capacity / Parameters (p) p = n

Classical Regime (p<np < np<n)

  • In classical statistics, as model capacity (number of parameters ppp) increases relative to the number of training samples nnn, bias decreases while variance increases.
  • The test error exhibits the standard U-shaped curve, reaching an optimal trade-off point and then increasing due to overfitting as p→np \to np→n.

The Interpolation Threshold (p=np = np=n)

  • At the interpolation boundary where model capacity just barely matches the training set size, the model fits the training data and noise with zero training loss.
  • To fit noisy training labels exactly without excess capacity, the model must contort its decision boundary violently (large norm solutions), driving the variance to its maximum. This causes a pronounced spike in test error.

Modern Overparameterized Regime (p≫np \gg np≫n)

  • When capacity extends well beyond the interpolation point (p≫np \gg np≫n), there are infinitely many parameter configurations that achieve zero training error.
  • Optimizers like Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) implicitly regularize the solution by selecting the interpolating function with the minimum norm (e.g., minimum L2L_2L2​ norm in weights): w∗=arg⁡min⁡w∥w∥s.t.Xw=y w^* = \arg\min_w \Vert{}w\Vert{} \quad \text{s.t.} \quad Xw = y w∗=argwmin​∥w∥s.t.Xw=y
  • As parameter count increases further, the space of zero-loss interpolators expands, allowing SGD to find smoother, lower-norm functions that interpolate the training points while generalizing effectively.

Double descent manifests across three primary dimensions:

  1. Model-wise Double Descent: Varying the width or depth of the architecture.
  2. Epoch-wise Double Descent: Prolonged training where error drops, rises, and drops again.
  3. Sample-wise Double Descent: Varying dataset size nnn for a fixed model size ppp.
